scenarios.title: 80 m Gap
scenarios.predictionPrompt: Does shorter reaction time alone guarantee a shorter total stop across different speeds?
predictions: Only after considering speed and braking travel
Reaction distance is the whole stopping distance
scenarios.explanationPrompt: Explain the separate reaction and braking contributions, using units and the stationary-obstacle model.
scenarios.keyIdea: Reaction travel is v × t. Braking travel uses the supplied consistent model; slope shows speed.
hints: Multiply speed by reaction time for reaction travel. Braking distance is supplied separately.
Add reaction and braking travel. Clearance = obstacle gap − total stop; zero means reaching its position.
scenarios.teacherReasoning: 20×1.5 = 30 m reaction; add 40 m braking for 70 m total. The 80 m obstacle leaves 10 m in this illustrative model.

scenarios.title: 45 m Gap
scenarios.predictionPrompt: Do you predict that the vehicle stops before the 45 m obstacle after reaction and braking?
scenarios.explanationPrompt: Explain the separate reaction and braking contributions, using units and the stationary-obstacle model.
scenarios.keyIdea: Reaction travel is v × t. Braking travel uses the supplied consistent model; slope shows speed.
hints: Multiply speed by reaction time for reaction travel. Braking distance is supplied separately.
Add reaction and braking travel. Clearance = obstacle gap − total stop; zero means reaching its position.
scenarios.teacherReasoning: 15×1 = 15 m reaction; plus 22.5 m braking gives 37.5 m. Clearance is 45−37.5 = 7.5 m.

scenarios.title: Same Speed, Different Reaction Time
scenarios.answer: Reaction travel changes linearly; braking distance stays supplied and unchanged.
scenarios.predictionPrompt: At unchanged speed and braking conditions, what does a longer reaction time change?
scenarios.explanationPrompt: Compare reaction distances for the three supplied times and explain why braking distance stays unchanged when speed and braking conditions stay fixed.
scenarios.keyIdea: At constant speed, reaction travel changes linearly with reaction time; the supplied braking distance stays unchanged.
hints: Multiply speed by reaction time for reaction travel. Braking distance is supplied separately.
Add reaction and braking travel. Clearance = obstacle gap − total stop; zero means reaching its position.
scenarios.teacherReasoning: At 20 m/s, reaction times 1, 1.5 and 2 s give 20, 30 and 40 m. The supplied 40 m braking distance stays fixed.

scenarios.title: Graph Reading
scenarios.answer: Slope represents speed; the horizontal segment means the vehicle is stopped.
scenarios.predictionPrompt: What does a horizontal distance-time segment mean?
scenarios.explanationPrompt: Explain what graph slope represents, why it decreases during braking, and why the horizontal segment shows the vehicle is stopped.
scenarios.keyIdea: Distance-time slope is speed. Constant deceleration gives a curved braking trace followed by a horizontal stopped segment.
scenarios.teacherReasoning: Reaction slope is 20 m/s. During braking it decreases to zero; a horizontal distance-time segment means stopped.
